findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed during today’s inspection.
1. The stainless steel sheet sealing the edge of the wall behind the hand sink by the drinks station.
2. The tiles placement around the drainage system between the dish area and the cook line were observed broken.
3. caulking on the multi-compartment sink in the produce prep area was observed coming off.
4. The caulking sealing the countertop right of the dish machine was observed coming off the wall.
5. The stainless steel sheets in the utility sink were observed unscrewed and coming off the wall including the caulking.

PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that these areas are sealed appropriately providing smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Inspector observed a mop head being store in dirty water in a mop bucket at the back of the kitchen. PIC was made aware. The mop head was removed and stored properly. Ensure that mop heads are stored properly to allow them to air dry properly.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil with in the dish machine. PIC was made aware of the soil build up and PIC immediately got it cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the dish machine are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a few jugs of milk that had been opened a couple days prior without being date marked. Discussed with PIC and PIC wrote the “opened dates” on the jugs and ensured inspector that they will continue to monitor the date marking on food items. PIC ensured inspector that they will inform staff to observe date marking as well. Ensure that food items are clearly date marked if not used within 24 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

Ensure that mop is store in a position that allows it to air dry limiting the growth of bacteria cultures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

Throughout the inspection three separate hand washing sink are observed inaccessible for convenient use. One had several pans in front of it. The other two had items in the sinks preventing their use for hand washing. The PIC was shown and moved the items during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible to facilitate hand washing at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Throughout the inspection multiple food contact items were observed still soiled while in storage as ready for use. It appears that they have not been getting effectively cleaned at the dish washing station. The PIC was shown and moved the noted items back to dish for re-cleaning. It is highly suggested that education takes place with the dish washers to ensure that they review dishes prior to moving them to a “ready for use” location.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

The dish machine in the facility could not, after multiple attempts, reach the critical temperature of 160°F at the surface of the dishes. Both inspector maximum registering thermometer and irreversible temperature indicator as well as the facility maximum registering thermometer were used. The PIC called EcoLab for maintenance and they stated that first thing tomorrow maintenance would commence. The three part sink was set up during this inspection with sanitizer. The dish machine can be used to wash and rinse the dishes and the sink used to sanitize. This is a temporary measure and a follow up will be conducted to ensure that the machine is effectively sanitizing again.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

Multiple spray bottles and sani buckets in the facility would not register on either the inspector’s or facility test strips. These items were remade during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry.

The mops observed in the mop sink are stored with the heads pooled on the floor of the mop sink. The PIC was shown and moved the mops so that the heads would air dry effectively. Ensure that storage is maintained in such a way moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Multiple locations throughout the facility are observed with soiled caulking or caulking that is separating and not maintaining an effective seal. The PIC was shown the relevant areas and instructed to repair/replace the caulking prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Multiple drinks in the facility are observed located mixed in with foods intended for consumers. The items were shown to the PIC as they were found and removed to correct. Ensure that all employee foods/drinks are stored seperately from consumer foods so as to prevent possible cross contamination. The rule of thumb is generally for the employee item to be stored below and/or away from consumer foods.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: It was observed that there were skewers or other items in the handwashing sinks throughout the facility’s kitchen. Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for the intended purpose of handwashing. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not blocked and remain accessible at all times. CORRECTED- The items were moved out of each handwashing sink. 

 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There was a container of salad mix that was uncovered in the walk-in cooler. Ensure that all food is covered during storage to protect them from cross contamination. CORRECTED- The salad was removed and placed on the cook line for use. 

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Wiping cloths were observed to be stored on the cook line in-between uses. Ensure that if wiping cloths are not in use then they are stored in a sanitizer solution. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the wiping cloths into a sanitizer bucket. 

(B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following areas were observed with an accumulation of food debris/soils:

1. REPEAT- The bottom of the fry freezer along the cook-line has food debris and ice buildup.
2. The floor to the left of the ice machine. 

These areas need to be cleaned to remove the current accumulation of food debris/soil residues and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 

 (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The following maintenance is observed to be needed throughout the facility: 

1. The caulking on the handwashing sinks throughout the facility is either missing or in disrepair. Ensure that these are re-caulked and are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The bottom shelf in the walk-in cooler appears to be broken and needs repaired. 
3. The coving to the left of the office door is in need of repair. 
4. REPEAT- The walk-in freezer is observed to have ice accumulation taking place coming from the insulation around the pipe connected to the unit. Ensure that the unit is serviced in a manner that prevents the ice accumulation. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are repaired and maintained repaired. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: An employee beverage was observed stored on the surface of the salad prep station. This drink was removed from this location and placed in a designated employee beverage area that does not pose a contamination hazard. Ensure that employee beverages are stored between use in a manner that does not pose a contamination hazard away from food and food prep areas. This is a repeat violation from the 8/21/2023 inspection report and the facility will be receiving a repeat letter documenting the violation. 
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: It was observed that multiple bowls along the cook-line used to serve food items were visibly soiled after being sent through the wash, rinse, sanitize process. These bowls were pulled from service and placed back into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that service items are fully washed, rinsed, and sanitized before placing them in the ready to use service stations. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The ice scoops at the bar are observed to be stored in direct contact with the side of the liquor bottles in the side tray. This was discussed with the PIC as an improper storage method due to the hand contact with the bottles and then contacting the surface of the scoops. PIC is removing the scoops from this location and will be placing them in a clean and sanitized container for storage ont he side of the ice machine. Ensure these scoops are stored in a manner that does not allow for contamination between use. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The fry cooler along the cook-line is observed to have water accumulation in the bottom of the cooler. This item was discussed with the PIC to have the cooler serviced or to see if there is a drain line plugged anywhere. Ensure repairs are made to the cooler that prevents the water accumulation from taking place. Ensure that all food items in this area remain inside containers that create a barrier from the water accumulation and that the cooler is properly cleaned and sanitized to remove the current water buildup. This item is a repeat violation from the 8/21/2023 inspection and the facility will receive a repeat letter to document the violation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following areas were observed with an accumulation of food debris/soils:
-The bottom of the fry freezer along the cook-line has food debris and ice buildup.
-The walk-in cooler fan cages and ceiling are observed with dust accumulation.
-The shelving above the silverware wrapping station and the adjacent equipment leading up to the ceiling have an accumulation of dust.
-The walk-in cooler under the shelves and against the walls are observed with food debris/liquid buildup.
These areas need to be cleaned to remove the current accumulation of food debris/soil residues and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The walk-in freezer is observed to have ice accumulation taking place coming from the insulation around the pipe connected to the unit. The insulation appears to have split where the ice is most apparent. Ensure the insulation is repaired and the unit is serviced in a manner that prevents the ice accumulation. Until repairs are made, the facility has placed a metal pan to catch any further ice that accumulates from the unit. Ensure this pan is removed and placed in the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle at the end of each day and then placed back into this location until the ice accumulation is no longer occurring. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
